items.abstract:
<jats:title>ABSTRACT</jats:title>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Objectives</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>This study investigates the environmental contexts that influenced the evolution of hominin foot morphology, focusing on when, where, and under what conditions key synapomorphies evolved. We test whether shifts in ecological conditions are associated with changes in locomotor function.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Methods</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>We used phylogenetic and biogeographical analyses with paleoenvironmental data to evaluate the relationships between foot morphology and environmental context. Phylogenetic trees were inferred using the fossilized birth‐death model and time‐calibrated. Multiple topologies were used to explore alternative evolutionary hypotheses. Historical biogeography was reconstructed using BioGeoBEARS. Finally, environmental conditions at key ancestral nodes were inferred by linking reconstructed geographical regions with paleoenvironmental proxies.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Results</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>
                      The results suggest that the origin of bipedalism likely occurred during intervals of increasing aridity. Later in hominin evolution, wetter environments became more important, and most derived traits evolved during wet or mixed environments. The last common ancestors (LCA) of most
                      <jats:italic>Australopithecus</jats:italic>
                      and
                      <jats:italic>Paranthropus</jats:italic>
                      species likely lived in wetter environments, and the LCA of Homo lived in both dry and wet environments. Across all trees, an average of 5.3 synapomorphies evolved in wet environments, 5.0 in dry and wet environments, and 4.3 in mixed environments. The results suggest that a considerable number of foot synapomorphies evolved during periods of ecological transition.
                    </jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Conclusions</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>Ecological flexibility seems to be significant in hominin foot evolution, enabling synapomorphies to persist as hominins faced different environmental conditions. These findings illustrate how environments influenced the evolution of key adaptations in hominins.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
authors: Yeganeh Sekhavati, Thomas Cody Prang, David Strait
items.summary: 《人亚科足部演化的环境背景》：该研究用系统发育与生物地理学分析结合古环境数据，检验生态条件变化是否与运动功能改变相关，发现双足行走起源可能出现在干旱加剧时期，而多数衍生特征演化于湿润或混合环境，生态灵活性在人亚科足部演化中作用显著，值得关注。
items.title: Environmental Context of Hominin Foot Evolution

items.abstract: Since its publication in 2021, the discovery of hominin hand- and footprints at the Quesang site on the Central Tibetan Plateau has attracted widespread attention and sparked intensive discussion within the archaeological community. The site preserves evidence of human activity from both the Middle Pleistocene and the Early-to-Middle Holocene, which serves as a critical milestone for understanding how humans expanded into and permanently occupied high-altitude extreme environments. Given the ongoing controversies regarding the chronology of the Quesang prints, this study presents a systematic review of the formation mechanisms of thermogenic travertine and its associated geochronological methodologies applicable to such deposits. Furthermore, we conducted a series of supplementary experiments to rigorously address and evaluate the major concerns raised regarding the reliability of previous age determinations. Our results demonstrate that the U-Th ages obtained from the Quesang travertine are robust and reliable, and are fully consistent with the available geochemical, petrographic and stratigraphic evidence. These findings provide strong support for the established chronology of the Quesang hand- and footprints and reinforce their significance for understanding early human occupation of the Tibetan Plateau.

items.abstract: Southern South Africa houses some key archaeological sites, which document the behavioural and technological development of Homo sapiens . During Marine Isotope Stages (MIS) 5 and 4, this region experienced marked climate variability, particularly in temperature and precipitation. Therefore, this study advances on the region's past climate reconstructions to provide an environmental context for the archaeological findings. Radiogenic strontium (Sr) and neodymium (Nd) isotope, grain size and X-ray fluorescence (XRF) core scanning records from marine sediment core MD20-3591, located offshore the Palaeo-Agulhas Plain (PAP), southern Africa, document changes in sediment provenance between 90 and 50 ka, an interval within the Middle Stone Age period (MSA; 300 - 40 ka). The Nd isotope record reflects a combination of alternating riverine material from South African sources and that transported southwards by the Agulhas Current. Shifts in river discharge from the northern Limpopo to the southern South African endmembers likely resulted from local insolation changes, which caused latitudinal shifts in the Intertropical Convergence Zone (ITCZ). The Sr isotopes highlight additional contributions from southern South African sources on shorter timescales, reflecting local hydroclimate sensitivity. The XRF and Nd isotope record, together with climate model results, indicate an increased sediment contribution from the Limpopo River catchment during Southern Hemisphere (SH) summer insolation maxima, likely driven by southward shifts in the subtropical rain belts leading to increased runoff from this basin. Conversely, during SH summer insolation minima, sediment supply from the Limpopo River decreases. During MIS 4 (71-57 ka), a consistent pattern emerges of greater local South African sediment input at marine sediment core site MD20-3591, with coarser sediments likely being sourced from Southern Cape rivers due to a reduced distance from the palaeoshoreline at the sea-level low-stand, and enhanced sediment availability from the exposed continental shelf. This study is of interest for the regional anthropological record, as pulses of technological innovation may have been linked to fluctuations in hydroclimate and in exposure of the PAP, including the elaboration of complex toolkits and subsistence strategies by Homo sapiens .

items.abstract: The discovery of Homo floresiensis at Liang Bua Cave, Flores Island, in 2003 stands as one of the most revolutionary breakthroughs in twenty-first-century paleoanthropology. This small-bodied hominin species sparked global scientific debate regarding both its species validity and the possibility of pathological conditions in the discovered individual. This study aims to analyze the development of paleoanthropological interpretations of Homo floresiensis at the Liang Bua and Mata Menge sites during the period 2016–2026. A qualitative method with a descriptive-analytical literature review approach was applied to relevant international scientific publications. The results show that redating of the Liang Bua site revised the age of H. floresiensis skeletal remains to 100,000–60,000 years ago, eliminating the possibility of significant interaction with Homo sapiens. Fossil discoveries at Mata Menge, dated to approximately 700,000 years ago, confirmed that small body size was already present long before the Liang Bua period, strengthening the insular dwarfism hypothesis derived from Homo erectus ancestry. Various phylogenetic studies rejected all pathological hypotheses and affirmed H. floresiensis as a valid hominin species. Its extinction approximately 50,000–60,000 years ago was multifactorial, involving climatic changes in the form of seasonal aridification and possible demographic pressure from the arrival of Homo sapiens. This study concludes that Homo floresiensis represents compelling evidence of the complexity of hominin evolution and dispersal in Southeast Asia.

items.abstract: Micromammal assemblages offer valuable insights into local palaeoenvironmental conditions and contribute to refining biochronological frameworks in the Cradle of Humankind (CoH), South Africa. This study presents the taxonomic, taphonomic, and palaeoecological analysis of micromammalian remains recovered from newly excavated in situ deposits at the Gondolin GD2 locality. A total of 372 cranio-dental elements representing at least 124 individuals were identified, comprising 19 taxa across five mammalian orders. Rodents dominate the assemblage (≈78% of MNI), with Mystromys and Otomys being the most abundant genera, accompanied by representatives of Muridae, Nesomyidae, Bathyergidae, and Gliridae. Other mammalian orders are represented by Macroscelididae (Macroscelidea), Soricidae (Eulipotyphla), Chiroptera, and Chrysochloridae (Afrosoricida). Taphonomic analyses reveal high fragmentation rates and pervasive manganese coatings, but a very low frequency and weak intensity of digestive etching on incisors. These patterns closely match modern barn owl (Tyto alba) assemblages, indicating accumulation primarily by a Category 1 nocturnal raptor. This accumulation mode appears consistent with other CoH micromammal assemblages, strengthening the reliability of inter-site faunal comparisons. Faunal composition indicates a landscape dominated by grassland and open savanna habitats, with localised wet or riverine environments suggested by the occurrence of Dasymys. Overall taxonomic similarities with other regional assemblages support a degree of ecological stability in the CoH during the Early Pleistocene. This assemblage provides a new data point for understanding micromammal palaeobiodiversity, site formation processes, and palaeoenvironmental dynamics in southern Africa.

items.abstract: Territories, defined here as areas of prehistoric resource acquisition, are difficult to identify in the remote past, particularly for the African Middle Stone Age (MSA) where assemblages are dominated by lithics. This study aims to (a) introduce a new protocol for the identification of territories in the archaeological record, and (b) using this protocol, investigate whether territories were present in the Middle Kalahari during the later MSA. We achieve this through a comparison of silcrete procurement patterns and provisioning strategies across eight excavated sites in northwest and central Botswana. Applying a mathematical approach to geochemical data (verified through petrography) shows that silcrete was moved c.220 km to Rhino Cave, c.210 km to ≠Gi and c.45 km to White Paintings Shelter in northwest Botswana during the later MSA. This contrasts with distances of <55 km for five later MSA sites on Ntwetwe Pan in the Makgadikgadi Basin. Reconstructed zones of silcrete procurement for the two regions do not overlap. Targeted chaîne opératoire analyses identify distinct approaches to silcrete provisioning: specific forms of long-distance acquisition and some direct procurement at the sites in northwest Botswana and an expanded version of local acquisition on Ntwetwe Pan. Silcrete movement has previously been constrained to c.82–67 ka and/or c.58–56 ka for the sites on Ntwetwe Pan. Bayesian age-depth modelling for securely provenanced artefacts from ≠Gi and White Paintings Shelter suggests that silcrete was moved to these sites during the earlier of these periods. The silcrete acquisition strategies we identify were therefore likely coeval across our sites and continued at c.58–56 ka for selected sites on Ntwetwe Pan. From this evidence, we propose that at least two spatially non-overlapping territories may have existed in the Middle Kalahari during the later MSA. Rhino Cave and ≠Gi were potentially part of one expansive territory, with populations sharing silcrete sources around Lake Ngami. White Paintings Shelter may have been part of this territory or could represent a smaller range within this territory. The sites on Ntwetwe Pan either formed part of a second smaller territory, or the western limit of a larger territory. Differences in silcrete types present at other recorded MSA sites in the Middle Kalahari support these interpretations. Our proposal can be viewed as a working hypothesis to guide future research in the Middle Kalahari.

items.summary: 《中印度温迪亚高原北部中松河谷边缘的旧石器时代遗址：初步调查》：该研究对中松河谷边缘的旧石器时代遗址展开初步调查，有助于了解该地区旧石器时代人类活动与遗址分布，适合关注南亚旧石器考古的读者参考。
items.title: Palaeolithic sites in the periphery of the Middle Son Valley, Northern Vindhyan Plateau, Central India: Preliminary investigation

items.summary: 《埃塞俄比亚下奥莫河谷的上新世-更新世木材：对古人类学与古生物学遗址古环境的启示》：该研究通过分析下奥莫河谷的木材化石，探讨其对相关古人类学与古生物学遗址古环境的重建意义，适合关注早期人类演化环境背景的读者参考。
items.title: Plio-Pleistocene wood from the Lower Omo Valley, Ethiopia: paleoenvironnemental implications for paleoanthropological and paleontological sites

items.summary: 《西北非从旧石器时代晚期到新石器时代物理行为的转变》：该研究考察西北非旧石器时代晚期至新石器时代物理行为的转变，值得关注该地区这一关键过渡阶段的行为变化。
items.title: Transitions of Physical Behaviour from the Later Stone Age to the Neolithic in Northwest Africa
